title: 2026 Digital Defense Report | Security Insider
key_facts: Microsoft published its 2026 Digital Defense Report page saying AI is compressing attack timelines and making advanced capabilities more accessible.
Nearly 40,000 CVEs (publicly reported software flaws) were published in the first half of 2026, putting the year on track to roughly double.
The median time from a flaw being found in the wild to being weaponised has fallen to well below 24 hours, while enterprises can take 30 to 60 days to fix critical external flaws.

Microsoft Threat Intelligence sees AI used in vulnerability discovery, reconnaissance, phishing, malware and exploit development; one evaluation strung together 32 stages of an attack in a controlled environment.
Most complex real-world intrusions still involve meaningful human direction.
Between February and early May 2026 Microsoft Defender saw ClickFix-style attacker-supplied commands run on over 1.1 million unique devices, roughly an eightfold increase.
Microsoft flags model misalignment as an emerging risk as AI is given more agency.
quote_evidence: Nearly 40,000 CVEs were published in the first half of 2026, putting the year on track to roughly double.
The data shows that the median time from vulnerability discovery in the wild to weaponization has fallen to well below 24 hours.

Most complex real-world intrusions still involve meaningful human direction, but work that once consumed scarce expertise and operator time can increasingly be accelerated, repeated, or delegated to AI.
why_it_matters_hint: Microsoft's own data say the gap between a flaw appearing and being exploited is shrinking faster than defenders patch.
notes: Company's own report and framing; page text only, the full report was not read. Release date of the report not stated on the page.
